notes: GPUI VIEWS. The target UI framework is GPUI 0.2.2 (Zed's framework), not React, and you have no training knowledge of its exact API. Before writing, read: the finished panel crates as worked examples (rever-ui-traffic, rever-ui-menus, rever-ui-history: their src and examples/preview.rs show how views, listeners, hover, scrolling, popups, text fields, theme, strings and previews are done here), every file in rever-ui-kit/src, and vendor/gpui/src/elements/*.rs plus vendor/gpui/examples/*.rs for exact method names. Build view structs implementing gpui::Render that reproduce each React component's layout, sizes, colors and behaviors. Already ported logic to use as path dependencies instead of re-porting: rever-ui-state (chat_history, agent_choice, constants with the model and agent catalogs, Storage), rever-chat-core (permission queue and options), rever-ui-menus (popup menu, chip select), rever-tool-profile (profiles). The two stores in your list call the main process over IPC (`window.rev.*`): port them as structs with methods that take that dependency as a trait or closure argument (the host supplies it later; the preview supplies fakes). Selections and actions a view cannot carry out itself (switch model, open a conversation, answer a permission prompt) are emitted as GPUI events (`cx.emit` with an EventEmitter impl). Colors and sizes come from src/renderer/src/styles.css (tokens are in rever_ui_kit::theme::Theme; define a missing one locally and list it in your report). User-facing strings go through `rever_ui_kit::i18n::Lang::t(key)` with the keys the TSX uses. Keep logic in plain functions with Korean-named unit tests; a file gets the `Port of` marker only when its behaviors are all there. Preview: fill examples/preview.rs so `cargo run -p rever-ui-chat --example preview_chat` shows every view with fixture data, menus open (rever_ui_kit::preview::run; the window is unfocused and closes itself). Look at your work: while it runs, `scripts/capture-window.sh preview_chat /tmp/preview_chat.png` captures only that window; read the PNG, compare with what the TSX renders, fix what is off. Do not bring windows to the front, do not capture the screen any other way, do not run the `rever` app, and never run cargo without `-p` (other crates in the workspace are mid-edit).
